title: Arrival-profile-decomposer-and-token-cost-atlas
author: Ava Patel
description: Context and motivation: Long-tail latency and per-session cost spikes have been hard to attribute because arrival patterns (burst vs evenly spaced tokens) materially change batching behavior and KV cache effectiveness. This PR introduces two complementary observability features: the Arrival Profile Decomposer which classifies requests into arrival cohorts and attaches a lightweight arrival histogram tag to spans, and the Token Cost Atlas, a set of Grafana panels and trace-telemetry joins that expose token-level cost and latency distributions per arrival cohort and per model variant. Design highlights: arrival profiles are computed in the inference gateway using a sliding-window inter-token arrival sampler that emits a compact 4-bucket histogram (initial, burst, sustained, tail) as a span tag; the decomposer is probabilistic by default (configurable sampling rate) to keep cardinality low and ships a deterministic cohort label for rollups. Token Cost Atlas combines those cohort labels with existing per-token accounting to produce cohorted percentile rollups, cohort-level cost-per-token sparklines, and a small explainer panel that surfaces canonical example traces for each cohort. Implementation summary: added arrival profiling to services/gateway/arrival_profiler.go with unit tests; integrated tag propagation into tracer middleware; introduced a lightweight span_enricher that annotates token-cost buckets on sampled spans and emits a minimal JSON blob to the metrics pipeline; added a new Telemetry dashboard JSON for Grafana as telemetry/dashboards/token_cost_atlas.json and a console panel component for the Redwood Console under console/src/components/CostAtlasPanel.tsx. Alerting and tuning: new alert rules include a cohort-aware latency SLO rule that uses cohort percentiles to avoid noisy suppressions when burst cohorts naturally increase p95; we added a calibration job that runs synthetic arrival profiles (tests/synthetic/arrival_profiles.yml) to compute tuned alert thresholds per model and per region. Backwards compatibility and rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag feature.observability.arrival_decomposer, default off for existing clusters; default sampling 0.1 in hosted and 0.01 in Dedicated by policy. Rollout plan: staged canary to 10% of traffic in hosted with telemetry-only mode (no new retention cost) for 7 days, then increase sampling if signal is stable. Testing: unit tests for histogram logic and deterministic cohort assignment, integration tests covering span enrichment, and end-to-end synthetic tests exercising burst/sustained/tail profiles. Performance safety: profiler uses bounded memory and CPU; end-to-end perf runs show <0.3% p95 inference latency overhead at 0.1 sampling. Migration notes: no schema change to production traces; new span tags are opt-in and light. Reference tickets: ENG-1283 (arrival profiling), ENG-2367 (token-cost atlas), SUP-4521 (customer request to explain per-session spikes). This description contains the full rationale, implementation notes, rollout and testing plan, and calibration guidance.

review_comments: Diego Navarro: Can we ensure the cohort label cardinality stays bounded? Suggest deterministic bucketing with expiry. Author reply: implemented deterministic 4-bucket with TTL and a config knob, added tests.

Samir Gupta: Need a clear fallback if span enrichment fails to avoid increasing error budgets. Author reply: enrichment is best-effort; failures are logged at debug and do not affect request path, added integration test to assert no error propagation.

Lena Körner: Question on alert tuning, will cohort-aware alerts create alert fatigue? Author reply: added calibration job and per-model defaults, and dashboards include suggested thresholds to operator-guided tuning.
Diego Navarro: perf numbers? Author reply: microbenchmarks added; <0.3% p95 overhead at 0.1 sampling in canary.
Samir Gupta: Approve after small nits fixed (naming + comment). Author approved.
release_notes: Introduce arrival-profile decomposer and Token Cost Atlas dashboard. Adds cohort-aware latency SLO alerting and span enrichment for token-level cost explanations. Feature is behind runtime flag feature.observability.arrival_decomposer and sampling is configurable. See docs/observability/arrival-decomposer.md for rollout and calibration steps.
